paper.title: An Efficient Algorithm For Generalized Linear Bandit: Online Stochastic Gradient Descent and Thompson Sampling

unmapped: The set of K context vectors A_t is drawn i.i.d. each round from an unknown distribution (action set changes every round via i.i.d. contexts)
Noise is additionally sub-Gaussian with parameter R (rewards in [0,1])
Regularity: lambda_min(E[(1/K) sum_a x x^T]) >= sigma_0^2
Diversity assumption (Assumption 3): lambda_f = inf_theta lambda_min(E[X_theta X_theta^T]) > 0 for the theta-greedy arm
The learner knows c_1, c_3 (lower bounds on mu' near theta*), sigma_0, lambda_f and R (used to set tau, alpha, g_1)
settings.definition_quote: We consider the $K$-armed stochastic generalized linear bandit (GLB) setting. ... At each round $t \in [T]$, the player observes a set of contexts including $K$ feature vectors $\mathcal{A}_t := \{x_{t,a} | a\in [K]\} \subset \mathbbm{R}^d$. $\mathcal{A}_t$ is drawn IID from an unknown distribution with $\|x_{t,a}\| \leq 1$ ... $\mathbbm{E}[y_{t,a}|x_{t,a}] = \mu(x_{t,a}^T \theta^*)$ ... we assume $\mu(x) \in [0,1]$ and $y_{t,a} \in [0,1]$.

algorithms.name: SGD-TS (Online stochastic gradient descent with Thompson Sampling)

bound.expression_latex: \tau + \frac{7}{T} + L_{\mu} p \sqrt{\tau T} \left[2\sqrt{\frac{c_3}{\alpha}} g_1(J) + 2 g_2(J)\right] + L_{\mu} p \sqrt{\tau T} u \sqrt{ \frac{2c_3 g_1(J)^2}{\alpha} + 2g_2(J)^2} \sqrt{1+\log \lfloor \frac{T}{\tau} \rfloor}

symbols.tau: aggregation/exploration length, ceil(max{tau_1,tau_2}) from Eq. (tau), depends on d, log T, sigma_0, lambda_f, R, c_1, c_3, alpha
symbols.alpha_sgd: strong-convexity parameter alpha = max{c_3, d, log T}/lambda_f
symbols.g_1J: g_1(J) = (R/c_1) sqrt((d/2) log(1+2 J tau/d) + 2 log T)
symbols.c_1: inf of mu' over the radius-1 neighbourhood of theta*

conditions: rewards in [0,1] and sub-Gaussian noise with parameter R
tuning: tau = ceil(max{tau_1, tau_2}) as in Eq. (tau)

source.label: main_thm
source.quote: When Algorithm \ref{sgd_ts} runs with $\alpha = \max\{c_3, d, \log T\} / \lambda_f$, and $\tau$ defined in Equation \ref{tau}, the expected total regret satisfies the following inequality $\mathbbm E [R(T)] \leq  \tau + \frac{7}{T} + L_{\mu} p \sqrt{\tau T} \left[2\sqrt{\frac{c_3}{\alpha}} g_1(J) + 2 g_2(J)\right] + L_{\mu} p \sqrt{\tau T} u \sqrt{ \frac{2c_3 g_1(J)^2}{\alpha} + 2g_2(J)^2} \sqrt{1+\log \lfloor \frac{T}{\tau} \rfloor}$

results.notes: L_mu mapped to k_mu (upper bound on link derivative). R(T) defined via means of the per-round best arm, so pseudo-regret. Regret is the GLM-mean regret. Per remark this is O~(sqrt(T)).

conditions: sigma_0^2 and lambda_f treated as constants (O(1))

source.quote: Combining the choices of $\tau, \alpha$ and the definition of $g_1(J), g_2(J)$ in Equation \ref{g1}, \ref{g2}, we have $ \mathbbm{E} [R(T)] \sim \tilde O(\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Order statement from a remark summarizing Theorem 1; dependence on d hidden. Appendix discussion states O~(d^{5/2} sqrt(T)) if sigma_0^2, lambda_f ~ 1/d.
